page_title: A Simple Content-Based Recommendation Engine in Python

sources.entry: Python: _A Simple Content-Based Recommendation Engine in Python_

summary.title: A Simple Content-Based Recommendation Engine in Python
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a content-based product recommender in under about 10 lines of core Python, using TF-IDF over product descriptions and cosine similarity, with precomputed results served from Redis.
takeaways: Content-based recommenders use item attributes such as descriptions and can handle the cold-start problem where no purchase history exists.
Collaborative filtering uses who-bought-what data and generally produces more incremental sales, though the article notes content-based signals add little on top of it in most cases.
TF-IDF over 1- to 3-word phrases weights distinctive terms higher than common ones, and cosine similarity ranks how close products are.
The engine precomputes the top 100 similar items per product during train() and stores them in Redis sorted sets, so predict() is a simple lookup.
summary.summary: The author, Chris Clark, explains the difference between content-based and collaborative-filtering recommenders, with pros and cons of each, using an eCommerce scenario. He then walks through a content-based approach applied to a sample Patagonia outdoor clothing dataset of id and description fields. The method uses scikit-learn's TfidfVectorizer with 1-3 word n-grams and English stop words, computes similarities with linear_kernel (equivalent to cosine similarity), and stores the top 100 similar items per product in Redis. The full engine code is included in a Flask app with train() and predict() methods.
